findings.source_quote: τῶν δὲ μὴ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ζωὴ ἐν αὐτῷ.
findings.english_quote: but for those who do not keep his commandments, there is not even life in them.
findings.issue: The selected working Greek has the singular αὐτῷ, whereas the main text substitutes the plural “them,” identifying the people who disobey as the location of life’s absence. This loses the singular wording and its referential ambiguity, including the possible reference to God. Footnote e honestly discloses the difference, but retaining earlier English and citing a differing Latin reading do not establish fidelity to the selected Greek.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “but for those who do not keep his commandments, there is not even life in him.” Revise footnote e and the lexical decision accordingly, explaining that the Greek pronoun is singular and its referent is not explicitly named. Preserve the reported Latin “in them” as an alternative rather than the selected Greek’s main-text rendering.

findings.source_quote: τῶν δὲ μὴ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ζωὴ ἐν αὐτῷ.
findings.english_quote: But those who do not keep his commandments do not even have life in them.
findings.issue: Independently against the Greek, this sentence changes singular “in him” to plural “in them” and explicitly presents the assertion as those people’s lack of life within themselves. That resolves a referential question the selected source leaves open. The shared note discloses the singular, but neither that disclosure nor agreement with the standard edition justifies the substitution.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “But for those who do not keep his commandments, there is not even life in him.” Update the note and lexical metadata to explain the singular pronoun without deciding its referent; retain the reported Latin plural as an alternative.

summary: Both editions cover all five paragraphs and preserve the fear distinctions, salvation promise, necessity, evil/good branches, commandment-keeping condition, and speaker roles. Both require revision of the final plural pronoun to remain faithful to the selected singular Greek. The witness notes otherwise accord with the supplied bounded project report, including its distinctions between preserved wording, editorial supplements, and indirect quotation. This review does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscript images, certify exhaustive collation, or automatically approve the proposed replacements.
